articles.title: From Ukraine to Africa, drone dog fights now a reality
articles.summary: The rapid proliferation of attack drones and loitering munitions on modern battlefields is pushing militaries around the world towards a new layer of air
articles.body: The rapid proliferation of attack drones and loitering munitions on modern battlefields is pushing militaries around the world towards a new layer of air defence — using drones to hunt down other drones. The ongoing Russo-Ukrainian conflict, which is characterised by drone warfare, has been the biggest driver of this shift. Ukraine has increasingly relied on interceptor UAVs to bring down Russian Shahed-type one-way attack drones, a tactic aimed at conserving costlier surface-to-air missiles for higher-value targets. Sudan's army, using a Turkish origin Akinci drone, has even shot down a Chinese-made CH-95 drone operated by UAE-backed Rapid Support Force.Interceptor drones work by detecting, chasing and neutralising hostile UAVs, either through direct collision, small onboard warheads or guided engagement systems. Unlike traditional air defence missiles, most of these interceptors are cheap to build and can be manufactured at scale, making them an attractive option against swarms of low-cost enemy drones.Ukraine has become the primary testing ground for this emerging technology. Ukrainian firms such as Wild Hornets have fielded systems like the Sting interceptor, built specifically to pursue and destroy incoming attack drones. Kyiv has also been linking interceptor UAVs to radar networks and command systems to sharpen detection, tracking and engagement.The next frontier is autonomous interception. In June 2026, Ukraine's Brave1 defence innovation programme confirmed the combat testing of an AI-assisted system, which fuses radar data with onboard recognition software to track Shahed-type drones while keeping a human in the loop.This area of warfare, like others is also experiencing an arms race where the development of a system leads to a counter-system and this cycle continues with each side one upping the other. In this scenario, newer jet-powered attack drones are cutting down reaction time, forcing Ukraine to develop faster interceptors and sharper guidance systems. Swarm tactics, jamming and the difficulty of spotting low-flying drones greatly add to the complications.Other major powers are pursuing similar systems. The United States has deployed its Merops counter-drone system along NATO's eastern flank and tested the Bumblebee interceptor, which uses automatic target recognition. Israel and several European nations are also building out aerial interception capabilities as part of broader counter-drone architectures.India, too, is building its own answer to the threat. The DRDO-BEL D4 system combines radar, electro-optical sensors and electronic warfare to detect and neutralise hostile UAVs, though this remains distinct from a dedicated interceptor drone built to physically engage airborne targets. Separately, DRDO completed development trials of its Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Launched Precision Guided Missile-V3 in May 2026, covering both air-to-air and air-to-ground modes, this step that could feed into future aerial interception and can be deployed as an anti-drone weapon.The learnings from Operation Sindoor have provided greater impetus to indigenous unmanned platforms and counter-UAS systems, as India works towards a layered defence combining radars, electronic warfare, interceptor drones, low-cost missiles and conventional weapons.

articles.title: Jamui molestation case: Tejashwi Yadav accuses Bihar CM of violating POCSO by sharing victim’s photo
articles.summary: PATNA: Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary on Thursday drew criticism from the opposition RJD for allegedly revealing the identity of a minor girl who
articles.body: PATNA: Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary on Thursday drew criticism from the opposition RJD for allegedly revealing the identity of a minor girl who was molested a few days ago in Jamui district.The minor, along with her family, met Choudhary and was assured of “speedy justice” and “strongest possible punishments to all culprits within a month through speedy trial”, officials said.Choudhary shared a photograph of himself with the victim and her family members on his X handle.The post was subsequently taken down, news agency PTI reported.RJD national working president Tejashwi Yadav saved a screenshot of the post and targeted the BJP leader.Sharing the screenshot on X, Yadav, the leader of the opposition in the state assembly, criticised the chief minister, calling him “foolish and inept”.He accused Choudhary of “violating the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act”.Yadav, who is also a former deputy chief minister, alleged that Choudhary had failed in his Class VII exam and was convicted in seven murders, PTI reported.“The BJP leader deserves the strongest possible punishment for violating provisions of the POCSO Act,” Yadav said.“The way chief minister Samrat Choudhary has violated the POCSO Act. Bihar Police should immediately invoke the POCSO Act against him,” Yadav said.He further questioned, “If the police have invoked the Act against 80-90 people in Jamui and elsewhere, why is the Chief Minister being spared?”The screenshot was also shared by Yadav’s eldest sister, Misa Bharti, the RJD MP from Patliputra. She urged the Bihar Police to “lodge an FIR against the CM,” PTI reported.Bharti alleged that Choudhary revealed the identity of the minor victim even as those who had uploaded videos of the molestation were being booked by the Bihar Police for violating the girl’s privacy.What happened in Jamui?The minor girl, a Class 10 student, and a Class 10 boy, both friends and residents of Jamui town, were returning from coaching classes on a scooter on September 19 when a group of youths allegedly stopped them in the Sadar police station area.The girl was allegedly surrounded and the boy was separated from her.Videos that later surfaced online purportedly showed several youths questioning the girl, subjecting her to inappropriate physical contact and allegedly dragging her on the road.Police said the episode was believed to have continued for around 20 minutes, though only portions were captured in the videos.The incident was not initially reported to police by the victims or their families.Police took cognisance after the footage surfaced on social media, traced the victims using a vehicle registration number visible in the video and registered an FIR under the POCSO Act and relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).All accused in the case have been arrested.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Patna | Silver Rate in Patna | Bank Holidays in Patna | Public Holidays in Patna | Patna AQI | Weather in Patna | Petrol Price in Patna | Diesel Price in Patna | CNG Price in Patna | LPG Price in PatnaStay updated with the latest Patna news. articles.title: Aasu protests over poor condition of NH-37 & NH-38 at Makum, seeks repairs
articles.summary: AASU protests in Makum, demanding urgent repairs to NH-37 and NH-38 over potholes and damaged stretches; calls for inspection and regular maintenance.
articles.body: Dibrugarh: All Assam Students’ Union (Aasu) members demonstrated in Makum on Friday, demanding repairs to National Highways 37 and 38.Aasu members took out a procession through the town and raised slogans for urgent action from the authorities. Makum Aasu president Deep Das and general secretary Rupjyoti Bhowmik led the protest.The protesters alleged that potholes and damaged road surfaces were inconveniencing commuters and motorists, particularly near the busy Makum junction.“The condition of the highways has been causing serious problems for commuters. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Friday welcomed the first ascent mountaineering expedition team, which successfully summited 20 previously unclimbed peaks above 6,000 meters in Ladakh in just 23 days.The flag-in ceremony was held at Kartavya Bhavan-2 in New Delhi, in the presence of the defence minister and other senior officials.According to the defence ministry, the expedition was carried out by a team of 20 highly skilled climbers from the National Institute of Mountaineering and Adventure Sports (NIMAS), Dirang, led by Col Ranveer Singh Jamwal.Speaking with the team, Rajnath praised the climbers' courage and determination in achieving this historic feat, calling the expedition a reflection of India's excellence and leadership in mountaineering and adventure sports.He described the climbers as a source of inspiration, noting that their successful ascents had set new benchmarks and would motivate young mountaineers across the country to take up adventure and exploration while bringing pride to the nation.The ministry applauded the expedition group's planning, technical skill, endurance and teamwork, and said it highlighted the country's high-altitude mountaineering capabilities and reinforced its standing on the global mountaineering map.This is the first-ever recorded summit of 20 unclimbed peaks in Chamser-Lungser, Gyama Nala, and ⁠Chokula areas in Ladakh Range," the ministry said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A Texas oil geologist first saw McKittrick Canyon in 1921, later bought the land for a private retreat; 38 years later he donated 4,942 acres and his home, helping create Guadalupe Mountains National Park

articles.body: In 1921, Texas oil geologist Wallace Pratt travelled into a remote, wind-swept oasis in West Texas and fell in love with its tall limestone walls and bright autumn colours. Thirty-eight years later, his long love for McKittrick Canyon helped change the future of Texas conservation. Pratt gave his home and thousands of acres to the federal government, creating the core of what would become Guadalupe Mountains National Park.First encounter with a hidden oasisPratt was working as an oil geologist for Humble Oil Company when he first visited the region. He was on a business trip in 1921 when an associate, Judge Drane, introduced him to the Guadalupe Mountains. Pratt was soon given a chance to see McKittrick Canyon, which was described to him as “the most beautiful spot in Texas.” According to National Park Service history records, he was deeply impressed by both the scenery and the geology. The canyon cuts through part of the ancient Capitan Reef, a huge fossil reef formed about 265 million years ago. The reef developed when this part of Texas was covered by a tropical sea. For Pratt, who spent his career studying rocks and underground formations, the canyon was both a scientific treasure and a peaceful place to escape. Pratt soon decided to buy land there. He and two business partners purchased ranch property in the area. By 1930, Pratt had bought the remaining interests from his original partners and continued adding land, including the lower part and mouth of McKittrick Canyon. He called the property Manzanital Ranch.Building in the desert wildernessBy 1931, Pratt and his wife, Pearl Stuckey, had built a small stone cabin inside McKittrick Canyon. The cabin was designed by architect John Staubs and built during the winter of 1931 to 1932. Made from local stone, it became the Pratt family's summer home. The cabin was beautiful but its location had problems. The narrow canyon could be hit by strong floods and bad weather. Pratt began looking for a safer site on higher ground. After Pearl died in 1940, Pratt married Iris Calderhead in 1941. Calderhead was a prominent supporter of the women's suffrage movement and had been involved with the National Woman's Party. Soon after their marriage, the couple began planning a second home outside the canyon. They chose a site southeast of the canyon mouth. The New York City architecture firm Milliken & Bevin designed the house. Planning began in 1941, construction started in 1942, and the house was completed by 1943. The unusual home became known as “Ship on the Desert” because its long shape and modern design made it look like an oil tanker. It used local limestone and large areas of glass to connect the house with the surrounding landscape. The National Park Service describes it as an early example of modernist architecture in the remote West Texas region. The house also reflected the lives of both owners. Its ship-like design was a tribute to Pratt's career in the oil industry. An oil tanker, the Wallace E. Pratt, had been named after him in 1937. A bright purple front door was a nod to Iris Pratt's work for women's suffrage, since purple was one of the colours linked to the suffrage movement and the National Woman's Party.A landmark gift to the nationWallace and Iris Pratt lived at Ship on the Desert for about fifteen years. Their life there was quiet and remote. The house had no telephone or television during their years of occupation, but the family enjoyed the wide desert views and sunsets from the property. Although the Pratts were officially retired by 1945, Wallace continued to work from an office in Carlsbad, New Mexico. He often flew his small plane from a private runway near the house to his office. The family also operated Manzanital Ranch from the property, and Pratt's children and grandchildren often visited during the 1940s and 1950s. By the early 1960s, the Pratts moved to Tucson, Arizona, as Iris's health declined and the couple needed better access to medical care. Pratt had already begun thinking about the future of his land. He wanted McKittrick Canyon and the Guadalupe Mountains to remain protected. In 1959, Pratt began donating his property to the federal government. His first gift included 4,942 acres of land and Ship on the Desert. Between 1960 and 1961, the Pratt family donated another 690 acres. The total contribution reached more than 5,600 acres. National Park Service records describe Pratt's land as the starting point for the creation of Guadalupe Mountains National Park.The foundation of a national parkFederal officials saw the value of Pratt's gift and continued working to protect a much larger part of the Guadalupe Mountains. The government later acquired additional land, including a large holding owned by J. C. Hunter Jr., to build the larger park. Congress approved legislation for Guadalupe Mountains National Park in 1966. The land transfer was completed by 1970, and the park was formally dedicated and opened to the public in September 1972. Today, Guadalupe Mountains National Park protects 86,416 acres of desert, canyons, mountains, and other high-country landscapes. The park includes Guadalupe Peak, the highest point in Texas. Pratt's original property became an important part of that larger protected area. His decision to give up his private land helped make it possible for the public to experience the landscape he had come to value so deeply.Preservation and public accessThe buildings Pratt created remain important historic parts of the national park. Pratt Cabin, located at the meeting point of the North and South branches of McKittrick Canyon, is now an interpretive site and rest stop for hikers. The National Park Service uses the cabin to tell the story of the Pratt family and their years in the canyon. Ship on the Desert is also preserved by the National Park Service. The house is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and is recognised as an early example of modernism in West Texas. It is generally closed to the public because of preservation needs. The house still shows the personal touches that connected Pratt's life to the building. Its long form recalls the oil tanker named for him, while its purple front door reflects Iris Pratt's connection to the women's suffrage movement. McKittrick Canyon remains an important place for geologists because its exposed rock layers reveal the structure of the ancient Permian reef. articles.title: UK steps up Palestine aid with £88m package for healthcare, clean water in Gaza
articles.summary: The UK government has unveiled an £88 million aid package aimed at providing crucial healthcare, clean water, and humanitarian support to Palestinians in Gaza. This initiative seeks to address medical needs and promote hygiene and sanitation amidst ongoing challenges in the region.
articles.body: The British Government has announced an £88 million aid package to provide healthcare, clean water and protection to hundreds of thousands of Palestinians.The funding will support medical consultations, mental health services and rehabilitation for children who have suffered blast injuries. It will also cover waste management, sanitation and hygiene services.The package is part of the £127 million allocated to Palestine under the UK's Official Development Assistance budget for the 2026/27 financial year.Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband called for civilians in Gaza to have unhindered access to humanitarian aid and urged the Israeli government to lift what he described as “unacceptable restrictions” on Gaza.“It is vital that civilians in Gaza have unhindered access to aid,” Miliband said.“The UK is pledging a major new package of aid to provide much needed healthcare support to those desperately in need.”He added: “We urge the government of Israel to listen to our call to action and take steps to end its unacceptable restrictions on Gaza.”The announcement comes amid a reset in the UK's diplomatic ties with Benjamin Netanyahu's administration. The UK had previously banned goods produced in Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.Israel and the US criticised that policy, while Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar announced retaliatory measures that included closing the UK consulate in Jerusalem and imposing entry bans on 11 British MPs.You use AI every day.
